name: spec-parity-gate-validation
cmd: scripts/spec_parity.py (negative control then green run), Qwen3.5-0.8B + r3lax DSpark draft, Metal
hypothesis: negative control (draft arm temp 0.3) reports >=1 mismatch and exits 1; green run reports zero mismatches, accept rate > 0, both arms print decode tok/s
result: negative control: 4/4 mismatches, exit 1 (red confirmed). green run: 7/8 mismatches at tokens 13-50, exit 1 (PARITY FAILED). accept_rate 0.655 derived, baseline 294.6 tok/s vs draft 100.5.
finding: The gate works in both directions: it detects the injected negative-control divergence and caught a real correctness bug in the Metal DSpark verify path. The default pairing (Qwen3.5-0.8B + DSpark) is not correctness-preserving. Both Markov and DSPARK_NO_MARKOV=1 draft paths diverge identically (7/8, tokens 13-50), ruling out the draft head — every emitted token is a target argmax. The drift accumulates over steps (absent at token 0), consistent with GDR recurrent-state drift in the hybrid target's batched verify forward vs the per-token decode forward.
decision: The gate is the admission test for Metal draft pairings: spec_parity.py must pass zero-mismatch before a pairing is used in a benchmark or default. Runtime fix (GDR recurrence numerics or post-rollback recompute) is a separate work item. Errors entry: docs/experience/errors/2026-09-09-dspark-draft-metal-parity-drift.md

name: doctor-solve-tolerance-35b
cmd: arle --doctor --model-path mlx-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit; arle serve same model; measure phys_footprint
hypothesis: printed weights+headroom+reserve+KV solve matches measured resident bytes within a tolerance small enough to make the solve an audit tool
result: 35B: rejected by resource guard (fixed 38 GiB > 34 GiB max limit under swap pressure), no resident to measure. 0.8B fallback: printed fixed+KV sum 12 GiB vs measured phys_footprint 1.2 GiB (plain) / 1.5 GiB (draft).
finding: The printed fixed-plus-KV sum is a capacity ceiling, not a steady-state resident prediction. The ~10 GiB gap on the 0.8B is MLX allocation laziness: the KV pool (2.7 GiB) and GDR static state (4,770 MiB, one recurrent state per slot) materialize on first touch, and a short parity workload touches a fraction of one slot. The solve is an audit tool for the fixed set and the memory limit, not for resident bytes. The 35B resident measurement is blocked by swap pressure on this box (13 GiB swap used).
decision: Note 4 documents the tolerance as: the sum overestimates resident by the lazily-allocated KV/GDR capacity; resident approaches the sum as the workload fills the KV pool. 35B resident measurement deferred to a box without swap pressure (same deferral as note 1). Wins entry: docs/experience/wins/2026-09-09-doctor-prints-resource-solve.md

name: kv-tier-cold-page-read
hypothesis: A cold KvTierStore page fault (read + consume 21.77 MiB) fits one DSv4-Flash decode step (15.25 ms) on L2 host DRAM but not on L3 NVMe
result: L2 fault p50 2.31 ms (15% of budget); L3 fault p50 20.85 ms (137%)
finding: L2 read path is a 1us BTreeMap borrow; the fault cost is the host-side copy (18.9 GB/s). L3 read is IO-dominated (19.2 ms, 1.13 GB/s O_DIRECT) and exceeds the budget on its own.
decision: Per-page paging of active sequences from L3 killed; roadmap Goal 2 item 2 deleted. L2 path remains viable.

name: mtp-batch-shape-check
cmd: serve tc27-nvfp4-slice2 --spec-type auto --mtp-draft-tokens 2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --spec-max-batch 1 vs 16; c=8 staggered 32K-trace load; read /v1/stats mixed-step share
hypothesis: batched MTP verify does not hit the mixed-step scheduler stall that killed batched DSpark on quantized KV (errors/2026-08-22): mixed-step count and busy share stay within the per-row envelope
result: mixed_steps=0/0 (arm A spec-max-batch=1: 0; arm B spec-max-batch=16: 0); decode_busy_ms 1874.1 vs 1759.7 (~6pct, within noise — not a gain, c=8 single point not matched A/B)
finding: batched MTP verify does not trigger the mixed-step scheduler stall (errors/2026-08-22): mixed_forward_steps=0 on both arms
decision: proceed to full-model acceptance (needle_gate x3 + lever_gate + 32K chain c-sweep on Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4)

name: s30-gdr-op-boundary-ab
cmd: scripts/bench_local_metal.py (baseline c8ce2ca5 vs lane) Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit c=1 prefill+decode + lever_gate
hypothesis: extracting run_gated_delta_step shared launcher changes no dispatch math; decode TPOT and prefill TTFT within noise (matched A/B <=10%), needle ladder unchanged
result: c=1 4B hybrid after hot-path fix: TPOT 43.74 -> 43.66 ms (-0.17%), TTFT 807.5 -> 809.7 ms (+0.27%), B,L,L,B; first refactor was +3.1% because helper rebuilt array(T) per GDR layer (24/step) and extern used wrong threadgroup_y; fixed to share the per-forward T array and use qwen35_cpp_gdr_threadgroup_y; needle 0.8B 2/2 exact at 115/300/446 on the exact fixed binary and baseline
finding: the +3.1% was real and caused by the per-layer scalar array, not noise; after threading the shared gdr_t_arr the delta is inside the 0.4-1.9% serve spread. 35B unloadable: 18.9/20 GiB swap in use by other tenants, 38 GiB fixed req vs 14 GiB free
decision: ship; op-boundary helper must take the forward's hoisted scalar inputs; wins entry updated with corrected table; 35B wall-clock deferred to headroom box

name: ab252-dyn-dispatch-metal-c1
cmd: matched Metal c=1 A/B 13239bc83 vs ff8f3b9ce, Qwen3.5-4B-4bit, P=543 N=128 K=6, B,L,L,B
hypothesis: Box<dyn Any> inflight + dyn submit/poll adds one malloc and two indirect calls per scheduler step; c=1 TPOT change within +-10% noise envelope (wash expected; decode is GPU-bound)
result: TPOT -1.98% (44.78->43.90 ms), TTFT -4.7%; within base's own 8.7% serve spread and +-10% envelope; needle 6/6 exact both arms
finding: Box<dyn Any> inflight (one malloc/step) + dyn submit/poll add no measurable c=1 cost on Metal 4B; decode is GPU-bound; generated tokens identical
decision: Ship #252 without micro-opt; CUDA c=1 bench_throughput A/B recorded as pending-remote in the wins entry

name: metal-matmul-device-ab
cmd: bench_step_matmul backend=metal d={128,1024,2048} batch=4 iters=100 A=#366 vs B=#366+overrides (recorded after the run)
hypothesis: on-device backward matmul removes readback/upload roundtrips per step; expect faster at large d, wash at small d
result: median step_ms (A host-fallback -> B on-device): d128 0.322->0.282 (1.14x, wash/noisy); d1024 2.385->0.921 (2.59x); d2048 10.895->3.626 (3.00x). bench_step_matmul backend=metal batch=4 iters=100 x2 interleaved, release, local Metal
finding: device backward removes per-step readback+upload of a/b/grad; saving scales with d^2 bytes, so visible from d>=1024, wash at d=128. Registered after the fact: the bench ran before the ledger row was committed.
